### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/rest`, touching **84** documentable anchor(s).

**48** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a3d47c2c59dce84c1cb1a64abb0f07b16675ce0b`.

⛔ **11** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **6** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `enforceApiAccess (9 routes)`, `enforceAuth (23 routes)`, `resolveExecCtx (28 routes)`, `resolveProtocol (25 routes)`, `routeManager (23 routes)`, `readDeclaredQueryNumber (4 routes)`
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `created_at (literal, 38 pages)`
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **17** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a3d47c2c59dce84c1cb1a64abb0f07b16675ce0b` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `1d4469c2d5b8fbabdab8cbb187d215249a3028bb` — the merge of head `5a05b4bde69fb06eb4ec5a5bceb79f4cbf7f0674` into base `a3d47c2c59dce84c1cb1a64abb0f07b16675ce0b`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 1d4469c2d5b8fbabdab8cbb187d215249a3028bb && git checkout 1d4469c2d5b8fbabdab8cbb187d215249a3028bb
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin a3d47c2c59dce84c1cb1a64abb0f07b16675ce0b 5a05b4bde69fb06eb4ec5a5bceb79f4cbf7f0674 && git checkout -B drift-repro a3d47c2c59dce84c1cb1a64abb0f07b16675ce0b && git merge --no-ff 5a05b4bde69fb06eb4ec5a5bceb79f4cbf7f0674

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a3d47c2c59dce84c1cb1a64abb0f07b16675ce0b
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs a3d47c2c59dce84c1cb1a64abb0f07b16675ce0b` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `5a05b4bde69fb06eb4ec5a5bceb79f4cbf7f0674`
Local-runs: none

Rendered 2026-10-13T01:01Z by an isolated review inside the adopting seat's session, on PR #23116 at the head above (branch `claude/issue-23050-s1-data-action-endpoints`, merge base `965a1bfc72`). Inputs: card #23050's body and its four comments (ruling and triage `6126748916`, claim `6134225153`, `os-dev-report` `6135442258`, and the seat's ACCEPT `6135541164`, read as a claim under test), the PR body and file list, the net diff against the merge base (11 files, +1501 / −1184), and the check-runs on the head. Owed because the PR edits a gate in another lane (`scripts/check-route-envelope.mjs`, `domain:spec`, declared after dispatch as `6135513000` on #6017); the whole PR is judged, since "move-only" is the claim that makes that edit honest.

**Check-runs on the head, read 2026-10-13T00:57Z:** 41 names, latest run of each: 32 success, 9 skipped (label- or path-gated: Auto Label, Build Docs, Check Changeset, Check PR Size, Console Pin Gate, the dogfood shards, Dogfood Verify CLI, the packed-tarball smoke, Temporal Conformance), 0 failed, 0 still running. Test Core (3/6) and (4/6) were in progress at the seat's ACCEPT and have since concluded success. The gates this review leans on all concluded success: `Lint · docs & code guards` (hosts `check:route-envelope`, lint.yml), `Build Core` (hosts `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, ci.yml), `Spec property liveness` (`check:liveness`), `Type Check · workspace`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, and all six Test Core shards.

### ① Derived judgments

**Move-only — RIGHT, measured.**
- The method body: base `rest-server.ts` `:9108`–`:10136` (1029 lines) against `data-action-routes.ts` `:190`–`:1218` (1029 lines). `diff` is empty once one 4-space indent is removed from the base; whitespace-stripped, both sides hash to sha256 `bbe45e60…8314`. Not one token of the body changed: no route path, method, handler, status, envelope, or `enforceAuth` / `enforceApiAccess` / `enforceExportPermission` / `enforceImportTemplateGates` / `resolveExecCtx` call moved.
- The alias block: base `:311`–`:372` equals the module's `:96`–`:157` except `export` on the alias line.
- Everything else in `rest-server.ts` (14 hunks): the 20-line stub (host literal plus `.call`), one import line with a one-line comment replacing the `runImport` / `prepareImportRequest` imports, the 3-line pointer where the alias stood, the `#20061` comment ("three doors" → "two of the three", with a pointer), `export` on exactly 12 module-level declarations (a diff of the file's `export` declaration names shows 12 added, 0 removed: `UNDECLARED_WHOLE_NUMBER_PARAM`, `readDeclaredQueryNumber`, `IMPORT_JOB_OBJECT`, `IMPORT_JOB_UNDO_MAX_ROWS`, `newImportJobId`, `capImportResults`, `parseUndoLog`, `importJobUndoable`, `importJobToProgress`, `importJobToSummary`, `rowsToCsv`, `createXlsxStream`), and the removal of eight imports the move left unused. `answerImportTemplate` and `resolveSecurityService` are untouched (the one class hunk ends at the stub's closing brace). No line citation anywhere in the head tree points into base `:9107`–`:10137` or `:311`–`:372`.
- The `this.` reads in the moved body are exactly 13 distinct members, and the host literal supplies exactly those 13; the interface names no other.

**The published surface — RIGHT, nothing new is published.** `packages/rest/package.json` has one `exports` entry (`.` → `dist/index.js` / `index.cjs` and `index.d.ts` / `index.d.cts`); `src/index.ts` is named-exports only, unchanged base→head, and never names `data-action-routes`. So `registerDataActionEndpoints`, `DataActionRouteHost`, `ServerScopedDataRequest` and the 12 newly exported helpers are reachable from no published entry, and the root entry exports no new name. The private method and its JSDoc keep their position in the class. The byte-identical `dist/*.d.ts` (sha256 `991a8fc9…`) is the dev's measurement, not re-run here; it is the only outcome consistent with an unchanged entry file and a declaration bundler that emits reachable names, and `Build Core` plus the four Type Check jobs concluded success on the head. The `RestServer['member']` indexed accesses on private members compile (TypeScript permits them) and make a renamed member a build error.

**The pattern — RIGHT, no stale value is reachable.** `config` is assigned once, in the constructor (`:2037`), and read once, at the function's top level during registration. `routeManager` is assigned in the constructor (`:2038`) and swapped at `:5534` / `:5538` inside `registerMetadataEndpoints` under `try` / `finally`; `registerRoutes` calls `registerMetadataEndpoints(bp)` at `:4601` before `registerDataActionEndpoints(bp)` at `:4641`, so the literal captures the real manager, and all nine `this.routeManager.register(` reads sit at the function's top level, synchronous, during registration. `cancelledImportJobs` is `private readonly` (`:1997`), a Set that is mutated and never replaced, so the six request-time reads see the live object. Methods are late-bound arrow closures on the server, so a spy or double set after registration is still what the body reaches. `this` inside the body is only the host: the function declares `this: DataActionRouteHost` and is reached only through `.call(host, basePath)`. The dev's rule for later slices (a reassignable field read at request time takes a getter) is the right one; it is stated in the module header and the report.

**The gate edit, `scripts/check-route-envelope.mjs` — RIGHT, a split with each sum unchanged and no loosening.**
- `auditDialectOnly` refuses `got !== want` in both directions ("a NEW non-conforming body" above, "fewer than pinned — bank it" below). `Lint · docs & code guards` concluded success on the head, so the gate itself proved `rest-server.ts` stringError = 26 and siblingCode = 39, and `data-action-routes.ts` stringError = 13 and siblingCode = 15. 26 + 13 = 39 and 39 + 15 = 54, the base declarations.
- `dialectOnly` is the same key `rest-server.ts` carries, with the `ratchet` it requires (`#9559`) and none of the write-site keys it refuses to sit beside (`responses` / `ok` / `err` / `privateOk`). The body was held to the two dialect facts inside `rest-server.ts`; it is held to exactly those in its own file. A `responses` pin would be a guarantee these bodies never carried, added by a PR whose contract is to move nothing. Noted, not a finding: the module inherits a waiver whose stated reason (208 write sites, edited daily) describes the hot file, not a 1,219-line module; converting it onto `sendOk` / `sendError` is `#9559`'s business, not this slice's.
- Discovery makes the entry required, not optional: `discover()` walks `packages/` for every `*-routes.ts` plus `OFF_CONVENTION_MODULES`; a discovered file absent from `MODULES` is "NOT DECLARED" and reds, and a declared file not found ("moved or deleted?") reds too. Without the new entry the gate would have failed on this head.

**Every other re-pointed reader — RIGHT, each a re-point with population and sum unchanged, none a widened allowance or a lowered floor.**
- `execctx-consumer-census.test.ts`: sites keyed `file:line` over both files; 62 sites unchanged (53 + 9), 16 caught / 46 bare unchanged; mentions 77 → 81 with the four new ones being the forwarder (two) and the interface member (two); `siteOfStack` steps over exactly one frame, the forwarder's, whose line is pinned above 0; the §6 wrapper assertion keys `rest-server.ts`.
- `rest-server-query-number-census.test.ts`: both files form one population; the ledger is keyed by route or function and did not change a row; the unclassified message names the file.
- `rest-server-canonical-query-ast.test.ts`: `minQuerySlots` 4 → 1 + 3 under the same door rule (`noDoor: false` on both), each floor its file's measured count; the two by-name literals are asserted where they now live.
- `rest-server-docblock-position.test.ts`: the module is read under the same no-stacked-docblock rule with floor 4 (header, alias, interface, function); the original file's pin is untouched.
- `ui-view-route-identity` and `ui-view-route-tenancy` measurements: the reverse-check floors (above 40, and exactly 1 for `enforceEnvironmentOwnership`) are unchanged thresholds now counted over the same code in two files; the sliced per-registrar readings still read `rest-server.ts` alone.
- `authz-probe-blind-spot.census.ts`: the rest-server row's population reads both files, so 70 / 19 / 51 is unchanged; `this.routeManager.register(` stays 63 (54 + 9) with a new control of 9 on the module alone, so a reading that stopped appending the module cannot hide; `enforceAuth` 57 → 61 is re-anchored, the four new occurrences being the forwarder and the interface member (two each), with no call site added.
- `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/records-forms.json`: the clone item's source anchor now names `data-action-routes.ts#registerDataActionEndpoints`, where the clone handler is.
- The ADR anchor `packages__rest__src__rest-server.ts.json` pins `filterAppForUser` (ADR-0045), outside the moved range.

**Readers that still name the old home, in prose — noted, not a finding.** Two the dev listed: `packages/spec/liveness/crud_endpoints.json:59` (evidence anchor `rest-server.ts#registerDataActionEndpoints`, which still resolves to the registrar; `Spec property liveness` success) and `route_generation.json:27` (a `note`, not scanned). Two the dev did not list, found here: `packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts:2348`–`:2349` ("`ServerScopedDataRequest` in `packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts`") and `packages/core/src/utils/import-runner.ts:138`–`:139` ("`rest-server.ts` declares a structurally identical local alias"). Both are docblock prose; the substance of each still holds (`rest-server.ts` imports the alias and its delete-door literal is still typed against it); no gate or resolvable anchor reads them. Under Prime Directive #10 these belong in the acceptance notes, and two of the four were not noted. See ③.

### ② Semver level

`skip-changeset` and `Clause-②: no` match what the diff publishes, which is nothing: the `exports` map and `src/index.ts` are unchanged, no `.changeset/*.md` is added, routes and both route ledgers are untouched, and the 12 new `export` keywords are module-internal. `Check Changeset` is skipped by the label, as designed. No accept set, no public name and no spec key moves.

### ③ Boundary flags

Every deviation in `os-dev-report` `6135442258`, answered:
1. The stub kept — the claim's "the class keeps only the call" and its "the published `.d.ts` does not change" conflict, and the dev measured that shape A changes the declaration (the docblock and `private registerDataActionEndpoints;` would go). The stub is the only shape that honours the stronger order. Answered.
2. The narrower range — `answerImportTemplate` (base `:10139`–`:10253`, pinned in the `.d.ts`, spied on in tests) and `resolveSecurityService` (`:10255`–`:10281`, four other callers) stay and are reached through the host. The diff confirms neither is touched. Answered.
3. The alias moved — forced by a measured one-line `.d.ts` change and the card's ban on a second copy. Answered; it leaves the two unlisted prose pointers above and a value-level import cycle between `rest-server.ts` and `data-action-routes.ts` that no module-level evaluation reads across (the bundler folds both into one file; `Build Core` success).
4. Readers touched outside the claim's literal surface — all are re-points the order asks for; the two cross-lane files were declared after the fact (`6135513000` on #6017, `6135521429` on #6023), which is the runbook's shape and why this review exists. Answered.
5. One merge of `origin/main` (`965a1bfc72`) — the net diff reviewed is against that merge base and is disjoint from the merged commits. Answered.
6. `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` NOT MEASURED locally — `Build Core` hosts the gate (ci.yml) and concluded success on this head. Answered by CI.
7. The `-cmp` worktree — removed; no trace in the diff. Answered.

The two `open_questions`, judged against the seat's rulings in `6135541164`:
1. The `packages/spec/liveness` evidence strings — the seat ruled A (leave). No defect hides behind it: the anchor names the registrar, the registrar still registers those routes through the moved body, and the liveness gate resolves `path#symbol` by symbol existence, which holds. ESCALATED AS A NOTE, not a card: the same one-hop prose drift exists at `protocol.zod.ts:2348` and `import-runner.ts:138`, neither in the report. The slice that rehomes the alias (question 2) should re-point all four in its surface; the seat's ledger should carry that line now so it is not rediscovered.
2. The alias's final home — the seat ruled A (the CRUD slice moves it beside its doors or into one small shared module). No defect hides behind it; the interim home is a type-only concern for `rest-server.ts`.

Out of scope, confirmed: `check:platform-checklist` is red with the same 8 findings on base and head, none in `records-forms.json`; it is out of per-PR CI by decision and reads on #6023.
